results.reason: Issue 1 says the 10-Business-Day window under §5.7(b) for the First Schedule Supplement (received Sept 14) has expired, as shown by the Second Schedule Supplement letter. It explains that under §5.7(c) the Ferrovane non-renewal is deemed cured for Article IX and the §7.2(a) bring-down condition, so the walk right and the indemnity are lost.

The escrow agreement discussion covers only housekeeping (blank schedules, tax treatment, amount and period). It never identifies a narrower 'Losses' definition in the Escrow Agreement or SPA §11.11 control over escrow disbursement.

Issue 2 states that MSA §14.2 treats a >50% equity acquisition as an assignment requiring consent and that the 100% share sale triggers it. It notes the consent is not in Annex 7.2(d), §4.4 or §7.2(d), so Buyer could be obligated to close and then face termination or List Price repricing by its sole-source supplier.
The memo states the window closed on September 28, 2026, counting 10 Business Days from Sept 14, and that this was before the Oct 13 letter.
The memo states the $4,850,000 indemnity escrow amount.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Attorney. Each issue has 'Where it appears', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Section III, 'Open Points: Not Resolvable from the Documents / Client Input Needed', flags these items.
The memo expressly concludes there is no remaining termination right over Ferrovane and advises not to assert one.
The memo states the Tavinor consent is not in Annex 7.2(d) and is not a closing condition.
